title: AI-assisted Synapse Spark and pipeline migration to Microsoft Fabric from the command line (Preview)
summary: A Fabric Updates Blog preview announcement for two command-line, AI-assisted migration skills -- a Synapse Migration skill for Spark pools, lake databases, notebooks, and job definitions, and a companion Pipeline Migration skill for Synapse Data Factory pipelines -- both operating over REST APIs with support for lift-and-shift or migrate-and-modernize strategies.
audience: Data platform teams planning a move off Azure Synapse Analytics Spark and pipeline orchestration onto Microsoft Fabric who want a scripted, AI-assisted migration path instead of a fully manual rebuild.
why_it_matters: Synapse-to-Fabric migration has historically been a manual, item-by-item rebuild; this preview gives teams a repeatable, idempotent, REST-API-driven path with explicit blocker detection and two selectable levels of automation, which changes the estimation and risk profile of a migration project.
takeaways: The Synapse Migration skill covers Spark pools, lake databases, notebooks, and Spark job definitions; a separate Pipeline Migration skill covers the Data Factory pipelines that orchestrate those notebooks, and the two are designed to work together.

Both skills run from the command line over REST APIs, are idempotent (safe to re-run if interrupted), and explicitly detect and flag migration blockers such as C#/.NET notebooks and GPU pools with no Fabric equivalent.

Two selectable strategies -- lift-and-shift versus migrate-and-modernize -- trade off automatic default-resolution and minimal code changes against user-guided decisions and Fabric-native refactoring at each phase.

The Pipeline Migration skill starts with a read-only assessment and automatically remaps Synapse-specific constructs (linked services, datasets, global parameters, SynapseNotebook/Validation activities) to their closest Fabric Data Factory equivalents, but explicitly does not migrate triggers.
This is a preview feature and the migration skills are distributed as open-source tooling in a public GitHub skills-for-fabric repository rather than as a built-in Fabric portal feature.

claims.text: The Synapse Migration skill is a preview, command-line, AI-assisted tool that migrates Spark pools, lake databases, notebooks, and Spark job definitions from an Azure Synapse workspace into their Microsoft Fabric equivalents, given a source Synapse workspace URL and a target Fabric workspace.

The Synapse Migration skill's migration is idempotent by design, so it can be safely re-run if interrupted, and it automatically detects migration blockers such as C#/.NET notebooks and GPU pools that have no Fabric equivalent, flagging them for the user to plan around.

The Synapse Migration skill runs a fixed phase sequence: Spark pools become Fabric environments (upgrading runtime to Spark 3.5 / Runtime 1.3), lake databases become Lakehouses, storage paths are scanned to create OneLake shortcuts for abfss:// references, notebooks are migrated with automatic code refactoring, and Spark job definitions are transferred with configuration preserved, ending in a cross-validation and summary report.

As part of Synapse migration, a dedicated phase scans notebook and job code for abfss:// storage paths pointing at external ADLS containers and creates OneLake shortcuts for them, as an alternative to physically copying that data into Fabric.

The skill offers two selectable migration strategies: lift-and-shift, which auto-resolves all decisions with sensible defaults, migrates notebooks and job definitions verbatim with no code changes, and consolidates lake databases into a single Lakehouse; and migrate-and-modernize, which prompts guided decisions at each phase and applies Fabric-native code refactoring.

Under migrate-and-modernize, automatic code refactoring rewrites Synapse-specific APIs to Fabric equivalents, including replacing mssparkutils with notebookutils and TokenLibrary with notebookutils.credentials, along with path rewrites and removal of linked-service references, whereas lift-and-shift leaves that code unchanged for post-cutover refactoring.

The companion Pipeline Migration skill moves Synapse Data Factory pipeline orchestration into Fabric Data Factory pipelines, rewiring notebook activities to point at the Fabric notebooks already created by the Synapse Migration skill, and likewise runs from the command line over REST APIs starting with a read-only assessment of scope and blockers.

The Pipeline Migration skill automatically remaps Synapse-specific pipeline constructs to Fabric equivalents: linked services become Fabric connections, datasets are folded directly into activity properties since Fabric has no separate Dataset item, global parameters become a variable library referenced via pipeline().libraryVariables, SynapseNotebook activities become TridentNotebook activities repointed by GUID, and unsupported Validation activities are rewritten as GetMetadata plus IfCondition; pipeline triggers are explicitly left out and must be recreated manually in Fabric.

Both the Synapse Migration and Pipeline Migration skills are open-source, distributed as part of a public skills-for-fabric GitHub toolkit, installed via command-line setup plus az login authentication, and designed to work with GitHub Copilot, VS Code, Claude, and other AI coding assistants rather than being a built-in Fabric portal feature.
